title: BRAN overview
legend:
**Fig. 1 | BRAN builds one patient state from fragmented retinal, blood and clinical data.**
**a**, People in the final training fit by source role (circle area proportional to people). Counts, lower bounds rounded down to 20, are not summed because MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV may share people. A benefit of unpaired single-source training has not been established.
**b**, Retinal features (384 per photograph), 43 clinical values with masks and typed age form a 192-coordinate state in three 64-coordinate blocks, retinal-associated, shared and clinical-associated, which are not organ-pure. An absent source leaves its block to the learned prior (small states, pale). † Schematic, not participant records.
**c**, Native heads give 26 recorded conditions (4 of the eye) and 9 blood count values, also from retinal input, and the frozen state gives the red-cell axis and distance from health (Fig. 6). With retina and age alone, MCV and platelet estimates were worse than with age alone (Fig. 2c). Hb, haemoglobin. Hct, haematocrit. RBC and WBC, red and white cell counts. MCV, MCH and MCHC, mean corpuscular volume, haemoglobin and haemoglobin concentration. RDW, red cell distribution width. Plt, platelets.
**d**, Native linear heads read the posterior mean, auxiliary decoders reconstruct inputs, not pixels, and dots mark each objective's training sources. Dashed readouts are fitted later on the frozen state. Development estimates pool five fold-specific models (1,928 AI-READI participants), and the fold 0 model scores other cohorts. The predecessor model's paired held-out test did not meet its primary end point (Extended Data Fig. 1).
methods_notes: Methods notes for Fig. 1 (moved from the legend). Panel a counts are the sampled-people column of the E4 exposure receipt for the fold 0 continuation fit, BRSET at least 6,500 photographs. The eye feature extractor was adapted on 115,273 public fundus images, none from AI-READI. SICdb and Zigong did not train BRAN and are not shown. Panel b, the clinical branch reads the 43 eligible continuous values of a 59-position container with explicit observation flags. Typed age is reported, an interval, right-censored or unknown, with 7 features, and conditions both branches and both decoders. With no eligible physiology and no retinal photograph the model abstains, and age alone does not count. Panel d, the frozen adapted DINOv3-S/16 extractor returns 384 features per visible photograph. The retinal branch projects each feature vector with typed age through an MLP with gated mean and dispersion pooling. The clinical branch is a two-linear-layer SiLU MLP of hidden width 128 with a bias-free linear residual, after a 3 asinh(z/3) input map. A shared-posterior MLP receives both branch states and two availability indicators and returns a Gaussian mean and log variance, which is learned concatenation and not a product of experts. Private blocks are linear priors from the shared coordinates plus a residual when their modality is observed. Each tile of the state column stands for 16 coordinates. Decoders reconstruct 48 continuous clinical positions and the 384 retinal features. Paired records supply alignment, condition detection, target-erased blood count completion and reconstruction, clinical-only records observed clinical reconstruction and a target-erased native blood count objective, and retinal-only records retinal reconstruction only. No unpaired people are treated as a pair. Development estimates use 1,000 paired participant bootstrap draws within outer folds. INSPIRE, HiRID and KNHANES 2022 and 2023 were unseen by the encoder but scored before, KNHANES 2024 is a locked temporal test, and no external cohort holds retinal photographs.
